natural_language_statement:
Call a subset of positive integers admissible if it contains no $a<b<c$ satisfying $a(b+c)=bc$, equivalently $1/a=1/b+1/c$. Write $G=\{122,183,244,366,732\}$ and $B=\{122,183,244\}$. For a Boolean membership predicate $S:\mathbb N\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, let $R(S)$ replace its selections in $G$ by exactly $B$ and leave every other membership decision unchanged. If $S$ is supported in $\{1,\ldots,732\}$ and is admissible, then

$$
R(S)\subseteq\{1,\ldots,731\},\qquad R(S)\text{ is admissible}.
$$

This replacement removes the endpoint 732 while preserving the forbidden-triple condition. Together with the cardinality inequality it supports the finite plateau theorem.
